label: TEST - medical history YAML parsing
info:
Companion test flow for medical_history_import_flow.json (PLAN.md §2's standing rule — every live flow gets one, kept permanently). Exercises Node-RED's CORE `yaml` node (bundled with Node-RED itself, not a third-party package — but this is the first place any of this project's flows have used it, so still worth confirming rather than assuming) against a small embedded YAML fixture matching PLAN.md §19's documented schema, rather than depending on a real file existing at /share/lucius_medical_history_import/ on whatever HA instance this runs on — self-contained, portable, no setup required to run this test.

What this confirms: (1) the yaml node actually converts a YAML string into a JS object with the expected shape — encounters as an array, each entry's fields present and correctly typed (not stringified numbers, not missing nested fields); (2) core split on an array property behaves as expected, same mechanism the live flow relies on twice. If the yaml node's output shape ever turns out to differ from what's assumed here (e.g. it wraps output differently, or a palette update changes behavior), this is where that would show up first — re-run this after any Node-RED/palette upgrade that touches core nodes, not just after touching this project's own flows.

name: Set embedded YAML fixture (msg.payload = string)
func:
// Small, self-contained fixture matching PLAN.md §19's documented
// schema exactly (a trimmed-down real entry, same field names/types as
// ward_medical_history_import.yaml) — deliberately not reading a real
// file, so this test needs nothing set up on the target HA instance to
// run. Includes one entry with every field type the live flow's
// n_mhi_prep_push function actually reads (string, nested-ish evidence
// fields, an array for related_medications) plus a second, sparser entry
// to confirm optional/missing fields don't break parsing.
msg.payload = [
    'schema_version: 1',
    'subject: test_subject',
    'compiled_date: 2026-08-20',
    '',
    'encounters:',
    '  - id: test-encounter-1',
    '    date: 2020-01-15',
    '    date_precision: exact',
    '    date_note: ""',
    '    title: "Test encounter with every field"',
    '    category: cardiac',
    '    encounter_type: procedure',
    '    procedure: "Test procedure text"',
    '    reason: "Test reason text"',
    '    outcome: "Test outcome text"',
    '    evidence: mixed',
    '    evidence_note: "Test evidence note"',
    '    related_medications: [Amlodipine, Aspirin]',
    '    notes: "Test notes text"',
    '  - id: test-encounter-2-sparse',
    '    date: 2021-06-01',
    '    date_precision: unknown',
    '    title: "Sparse test encounter"',
    '    category: medical',
    '    encounter_type: diagnostic',
    '    reason: "Only reason and no other optional fields"',
    '',
    'symptom_context:',
    '  items: ["test symptom one", "test symptom two"]',
    '  note: "Should NOT appear in msg.encounters after extraction"',
    '',
    'open_research_items:',
    '  - "Should also not appear"',
    '',
    'source_documents: ["test_source.md"]'
].join('\n');
return msg;

name: Check parsed shape against §19 schema
Force readable text

info: Not a separate trigger — reuses n_mhit_parse_yaml's output. Confirms core `split` on doc.encounters produces one message per entry with msg.payload = that entry, same as the live flow's n_mhi_split_encounters relies on.
